Sexey's vision, values and ethos
Our vision
At Sexey’s, we work together with a determination to be exceptional in all that we do.
Christian Distinctiveness
The parable of the Good Samaritan Luke 10:25-37 is the biblical teaching that informs our seven core values and underpins the ethos and values of the school.
All members of our community irrespective of belief, culture, identity or personal experiences are encouraged to live their lives developing and demonstrating the seven core values that are the building blocks of our individual and collective character.
As a community we provide a range of experiences and opportunities for spiritual development, many of which are within our curriculum and can be seen within the curriculum plans.
Our values
We place students at the heart of everything. Each student is unique and special and joins us with their own individual skills, qualities and aspirations that it is our privilege and responsibility to grow, develop and nurture. At the centre of the school’s ethos you will find our Christian values. We have seven core values: these are the building blocks of our individual character and through these we grow and develop as individuals and as a community.
How were the Christian seven core values created and developed?
The school community as a whole identified the values that people had to hold true to and display for all members of our community to successfully work, live and learn together.
How will you see the seven core values being displayed and developed at Sexey’s School?
You will see the seven core values brought to life through all our thoughts, actions and words and in particular, how we demonstrate them in the same way the Good Samaritan did within the parable.
Our policies are shaped and informed by our core values, particularly the curriculum and behaviour and rewards policies. Throughout our website, you will see how we explicitly incorporate the seven core values within our curriculum as well as the more discrete and continuous development within our culture and ethos.
Other Christian teachings that inform our school values
I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full
This teaching is lived through the school’s unrelenting commitment to the quality of educational, care experiences and opportunities. Through the commitment we have to developing the site as an exceptional place to live, work and learn we demonstrate John 10:10.
“For I know the plans I have for you,” declares the LORD, “plans to prosper you and not to harm you, plans to give you hope and a future.
Jerimiah 29:11 is seen at Sexey’s School.
Exceptional pastoral care
Personal development
Careers offer and experiences
Staff CPD offer
Our ethos
Sexey’s is a learning community. We are ambitious for our students’ academic achievement. We pride ourselves in our strong staff and student relationships, ensuring that every student feels safe, happy, cared for and valued. Home to school partnership and support are essential in supporting students in achieving their full potential.
At Sexey’s we value the importance of learning through enrichment and extra-curricular experiences and we strive to provide a wide range of diverse experiences to enable students to develop important life skills including leadership, creativity and problem solving.
We believe we all have the capacity to grow and develop and that this happens in a nurturing and safe environment that we seek to provide at Sexey’s.
We are passionate about preparing Sexey’s students for a life in the ever-changing world of work: ensuring that they leave us with the qualifications, skills and experiences to make certain that they are ready for the next stage in their journey of lifelong learning.
We foster high self-esteem through a ‘can-do’ approach to life. Praise and encouragement, to believe that anything is possible is the rule.
As a school with a large number of boarders, we are first and foremost a community. At Sexey’s traditional values are important and as such the School Song, the national anthem and the school anthem (Jerusalem) are integral to school events and acts of collective worship.
Whilst Sexey’s is a Christian school in ethos and values we believe in freedom of thought, and opportunities for self development through experience are paramount. As a result we are open to the exploration of all ideas and attempt to promote an environment in which students feel safe to explore their spiritual and emotional needs as they search for meaning, joy, contemplation and connectedness as part of their initiation into adult life.

About us
Welcome to Sexey’s School, Bruton! Established in 1891, we are a Church of England, non-selective state boarding and day school for boys and girls aged 11-18, based in the beautiful Somerset countryside. We are part of Quantock Education Trust.
We are ambitious for our students’ academic achievement and provide an inclusive, friendly environment — producing confident young people that are prepared for life, both today and beyond school. We have a passion and determination to be exceptional in all that we do. At the centre of the school’s ethos you will find our Christian values.
We have 7 Core values that form the basis of our ethos. These are the building blocks of our individual character and through these we grow and develop as individuals and as a community:
Choosing a school – the right school, is one of the most important decisions you will make for your child.
Parents often ask us what is so special about Sexey’s and what makes it different from other schools. Our reply is that we view every student as unique; valued as an individual, but also part of a family. We are very much a family school, educating brothers and sisters from Year 7 through to Sixth Form. It is our belief that every young person has a personal talent that it is our responsibility to help discover, nurture and develop.
Respect
Kindness
Forgiveness
Honesty
Resilience
Success for the future
School days have a powerful influence on future success in life and we believe a Sexey’s education can give you the best start.
Our students not only achieve excellent academic qualifications, but they also enjoy a wide range of extra-curricular activities and receive outstanding pastoral care. However successful you are in life, to be truly happy and fulfilled you need to have successful relationships with others. We provide our students with the knowledge, skills, experiences and confidence to allow them to be truly successful on their journey of lifelong learning
A website can only give you a brief glimpse of school life. You are warmly invited to visit and experience for yourself what we believe to be a very special school. We look forward to meeting you soon.

Pastoral care
Pastoral care and the wellbeing of our students is extremely important to us. We have a determination to provide exceptional care, support and guidance to all members of our community. Mr Darryl Carpenter (Assistant Head and DSL) leads the Pastoral Team.
Pastoral Team
Pastoral Leadership Team
Pastoral Support Assistants
In Years 7-11 pastoral care is primarily dealt with by our form tutors, with the support of our dedicated pastoral team. Should you have any worries about your son or daughter’s well being, please contact their Form Tutor or Head of Year initially. Our boarding Houseparents, Assistant Houseparents and Matrons support the emotional wellbeing of our boarders outside of school and provide the key communication link between home and school.
In Years 12-13, the Head of Year 12 and 13 Mr McLeish oversees the pastoral care of students, with support from tutors.
Pastoral matters may escalate to the Assistant Head (Designated Safeguarding lead), Head of Sixth Form and ultimately to the Headteacher.
Our teaching staff are very experienced at helping young people, and students are encouraged to discuss their concerns with tutors. We also encourage parents to get in touch if they think something is troubling their son or daughter, however trivial it may seem – we view the partnership between home and School as integral to a child’s happy and successful education at Sexey’s School.

Safeguarding at Sexey's School
Sexey’s School is committed to ensuring the welfare and safety of all students. We believe that students have a right to learn in a supportive, caring and safe environment, which includes the right to protection from all types of abuse.
Staff are vigilant for signs of any student in distress and are confident in applying our safeguarding and Child Protection procedures to avert and alleviate any such problems.
Safeguarding legislation and government guidance says that safeguarding means:
The school’s Safeguarding and Child Protection Team consists of: Mr Carpenter (Designated Safeguarding Lead), Mr Allan (Designated Safeguarding Lead Boarding), Mr Clayson (Deputy DSL), Mrs Dunford (Deputy DSL) and Mr Moise (Deputy DSL).
The school’s Safeguarding Advocates include: Mrs Sampson, Mrs Rogerson, Mrs Mills, Mr Bomani, Mrs Johnstone, Mr McLeish and Mr Richardson.

Disclosure & Barring Checks
Sexey’s School meets statutory requirements in relation to Disclosure & Barring Service – all staff and volunteers who work with the school who meet the ‘regulated activity test’ (Freedoms Act 2012) are required to undergo an enhanced DBS check prior to employment.
The Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy is available to parents and students on the school website here. All staff members receive annual Safeguarding and Child Protection update training and are aware of the procedures for passing on concerns within school.
If any members of the school or local community have concerns about the welfare of a child in the school, please pass them on to the School Safeguarding and Child Protection Team.
All those who work for the School, including the Governors and any volunteers who have substantial unsupervised access to children, are checked with the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) in accordance with national guidelines.

Parking Permits and Car Share Procedure
Parking spaces are available for Sixth Form students in the school car parks.
To obtain a parking permit please download and complete the Parking Permit Request Form. Request Forms must be completed in full with car registration and insurance information for a permit to be issued. Please hand your completed form to Mrs Crombie the Sixth Form Secretary or email it to acrombie@sexeys.somerset.sch.uk
To ensure the safety of our students we have set up new car share procedures.
The procedures will allow parents to inform the school of any students permitted to provide lifts or accept lifts.
Please complete the following consent forms to give permission for your son or daughter to provide a lift or accept a lift from another student.
Consent to drive students to school
Consent to accept lift from a student at school
For more information please contact Mrs Crombie the Sixth Form Secretary on acrombie@sexeys.somerset.sch.uk

Sixth Form Open Evening
Sixth Form Information Evening 2026 - NEW DATE 12th November 2026
Sexey's will be hosting a Sixth Form Information Evening on Thursday 12th November, 5pm. To register for a place, please complete this form providing as much information as possible. The event will include a welcome from our Headteacher and Head of Sixth Form plus the opportunity to visit our Sixth Form and classrooms, meet our teachers and students and discuss your Post 16 options. We look forward to welcoming you! Please note the change of date of the event from Thursday 15th October 2026.

A Level Results 2026
We are delighted to celebrate the outstanding A Level results achieved by our students. Their hard work, intellectual curiosity, and commitment to learning have led to well-deserved success. Many of our students will go on to top universities, while others will pursue pathways that reflect their aspirations and strengths. Each journey is valued, and we are confident they leave us equipped not only with excellent academic foundations but with the adaptability and purpose to thrive in a changing world.
Mr Clayson, Headteacher, shared “Congratulations to the Year 13 students and their teachers who have worked hard and deserve these super results. Their commitment and determination they have shown throughout their time in Sixth Form has paid off and they should be incredibly proud of what they have achieved.
Today is an opportunity to celebrate their individual successes and the progress they have made. I hope they enjoy this moment and take great confidence from their achievements as they move on to the next stage of their education or the first steps in employment. For many, this will be the start of their university or apprenticeship journey.
This year we continue to see exceptionally high numbers of our students accessing a place in their first or second choice university. This is due to the high-quality advice and guidance that they receive from the team at Sexey’s Sixth Form. We wish every one of our Year 13 students every success for the future and look forward to hearing about all that they go on to achieve.”
We have an unrelenting commitment to high-quality teaching and learning at Sexey’s School and we are very proud that we have so many high performing A level courses. Sexey’s Sixth Form prides itself in the string staff and student relationships which underpin the high-quality teaching and learning. This year the school celebrates 100% A*-C in the following subjects:
Other high performing subjects included: Further Maths (86% A*-C), Biology (81% A*-C), Psychology (80% A*-C), History (80% A*-C) and English Literature (80% A*-C) . These achievements also highlight the breadth and strength of our curriculum offer.
In addition to A Levels, students at Sexey’s Sixth have the opportunity to complete an Extended Project Qualification (EPQ), allowing them to broaden their studies, develop independent research skills and gain additional UCAS points to support their future education and career progression. This year, an impressive 100% of students who completed the EPQ achieved grades of A* to B.
The top three highest attaining students this year were:
Morley Humberston has also attained a place to study History at Cambridge University, following A*s in History, Politics and his EPQ on American History and Politics.
Mr McLeish Head of Sixth Form was delighted to join students on results day and celebrate their excellent results and said “This has been a fantastic group of young people, and we will miss them and the contribution they have made to our school community. We wish them every success as they take the next step in their lives, using everything they have learned in their time here.”
Chrysta Garnett, CEO of the Quantock Education Trust, said “I would like to congratulate all of our students at Sexey’s School on their A-level results. These achievements reflect not only their hard work, determination and resilience, but also the dedication of our staff and the support of families throughout their educational journey.
I am incredibly proud of everything our students have accomplished and of the positive destinations they are progressing to next, whether that be university, apprenticeships, employment or further training. On behalf of Quantock Education Trust, I wish them every success for the future and look forward to seeing the contribution they will make in their chosen paths.”
Sexey’s School staff wish each and every Year 13 leaver every success and happiness as they leave us and we look forward to hearing about what the future holds for them as an Old Sexeian’s.

GCSE Results 2026
Today we celebrate the achievements of our Year 11 students as they receive their GCSE results. Their hard work, determination and commitment to their studies have led to well-deserved success. Yet again, our students have performed at an exceptional level and should be proud of their achievements in their GCSE examinations.
Many of our students will now continue their education at Sexey’s Sixth Form, pursuing A Level and vocational courses, while others will move on to new post-16 providers and pathways that reflect their individual aspirations and strengths. Every journey is valued, and we are confident that our students will take the skills, knowledge and experiences they have gained at Sexey’s into the next stage of their lives.
Headteacher Steve Clayson said “Congratulations to all our students on their GCSE results. These results reflect years of hard work, determination and commitment, and I am incredibly proud of what they have achieved. Today is an opportunity for our students to celebrate with their families, friends and teachers, before looking ahead to the exciting opportunities that come next. We are particularly pleased to be welcoming so many of our Year 11 students back to Sexey’s Sixth Form in September, where they can build on their achievements and continue to develop their interests and ambitions. Whatever path our students choose, I wish them every success and happiness for the future.”
Results highlights: • On average, students make greater progress in relation to their starting points compared to national averages • We continue to meet and exceed national benchmarks for GCSEs and are particularly pleased with another year of very strong Maths and English results • Over 75% of students achieved a grade 4 pass in English Language, English Literature, Physics, Biology, Computer Science and Religious Studies.
The following students achieved exceptional results, including 2 or more grade 9s:
• Ru Boyce: 4 grade 9s, 5 grade 8s and 1 grade 5 • Ricci Grant: 4 grade 9s, 2 grade 8s, 2 grade 7s and 1 grade 6 • Rhys Newington-Wise: 4 grade 9s, 1 grade 8, 1 grade 7, 1 grade 6 and 1 grade 5 • Woody Bindloss: 3 grade 9s, 3 grade 8s, 1 grade 6 and 2 grade 5s • Spencer Mowat: 2 grade 9s, 4 grade 8s, 2 grade 7s and a grade 5 • Noah Watts: 2 grade 9s, 1 grade 8, 3 grade 7s, a grade 6 and a Level 2 Merit
We are proud of the achievements across our GCSE subjects and the dedication shown by students throughout their studies. These outcomes are supported by the commitment of our teaching and support staff, who work hard to ensure students are encouraged to achieve their potential. For those continuing at Sexey’s, the Sixth Form offers a broad range of courses, alongside opportunities for enrichment, careers development and the Extended Project Qualification (EPQ). Students can continue to develop their academic interests while building the confidence, independence and skills needed for their future.
Chrysta Garnett, CEO of Quantock Education Trust, said “Congratulations to all of our Year 11 students on their GCSE results. They should be very proud of the hard work and determination that have brought them to this point. I would also like to thank Steve Clayson and the staff at Sexey’s for their continued commitment to supporting students and helping them achieve their potential.
“It is wonderful to see so many students continuing their education at Sexey’s Sixth Form, and I wish all of our students every success as they take their next steps.”
The school would also like to thank families for their continued support and encouragement throughout the students’ GCSE journey. To our Year 11 students, congratulations on your achievements. We are proud of you and look forward to seeing all that you go on to accomplish in the next stage of your education and beyond.

Bruton Community Fireworks Night Returns on Friday 6 November
We are delighted to welcome the community back to Bruton Community Fireworks Night on Friday 6 November 2026, at Elm Field, Sexey’s School. The fireworks display will begin at 6.30pm, with an evening of family-friendly entertainment, delicious food and spectacular fireworks, all raising valuable funds to support our local schools.
The event is made possible thanks to the generous support of our sponsors, West End Garage and Mendip Fireplaces, alongside supporting partners BForder Homes, Lodestone Property, Turner Windows of Somerton Ltd, Fein Collections and Volta Electrical. We are incredibly grateful to all our sponsors and partners for their continued support in helping bring this much-loved community event to life.
There will be plenty to enjoy throughout the evening, with a tempting choice of food and refreshments, including wood-fired pizza, smash burgers and hot dogs, hot and cold drinks, sweet treats and ice cream. The Bruton Primary School PSA will also be hosting a tombola for families to enjoy.
Early bird tickets are now on sale, with prices held at the same level for the third consecutive year. Tickets can be purchased from Sexey’s School Reception during school opening hours, with cash and card payments accepted, or from the Premier Store on Bruton High Street (cash only).
To ensure a safe and enjoyable evening for everyone, the event is alcohol-free and sparkler-free, and dogs are not permitted. The fireworks display will last approximately 10–12 minutes. Local residents are encouraged to share this information, particularly with pet owners, so they can make any necessary arrangements.
Parking is limited on-site so visitors are encouraged to walk to the event wherever possible.
We look forward to welcoming families and friends from across Bruton and the surrounding area for another fantastic evening of community spirit, entertainment and fundraising in support of our local schools.
Children under three: Free

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama productions | thriving theatre at Sexey's School, Bruton : Sexeys
pageCache.text:
Drama
Drama thrives at Sexey’s. By taking part in the Key Stage and Whole School Productions, students grow in creativity and push the boundaries of their imagination. They are conversant with modern theatre practice, attending regular theatre trips to London, Bristol and Yeovil. We welcome touring theatre companies into school for tailored school productions that complement the curriculum.
Acting and Speaking Tuition
The Drama Department provides individual tuition in Acting and Speaking. These lessons are designed to build student confidence and expertise with a range of performance and presentation skills. Students who wish to may take graded examinations in their chosen specialism at whatever grade they wish. All examinations offer students opportunities to demonstrate performance skills appropriate to their individual interests and aspirations. These sessions can also be used for audition coaching for drama school, professional theatre, film and television as well as developing communication skills, presentation coaching and working with students for whom English is a foreign language. Further information and an application form can be found here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music lessons, activities and clubs at Sexey's School : Sexeys
pageCache.text:
Music
Music in Sexey’s School is all inclusive – both in style and ability. Our musicians play an active role in the school concerts, services, plays and musicals, and there are a range of clubs available to those who want to try something different. Music represents the school throughout the community by visiting residential homes and carolling at Christmas time.
The Drama department staff regularly organize visits to musical concerts and performances throughout the South West.
In addition to their classes, students are encouraged to take music lessons during school time. We have a wealth of expertise in our peripatetic staff who offer vocal Coaching, Woodwind, Strings, Drums and Piano.
For more information, please refer to our instrumental lesson request form or contact the Music Department.

The Bint Shield Competition
Sexey’s School’s Bint Shield competition is a core part of our School history. The shield trophy was first awarded in 1924 to the winners of the Inter-House Championship, which is a competition that runs throughout the school year. Everyone in the school community is involved and events can include sport, culture, theatre, science, art, music and all other school subjects.
Did you know?
Who was Bint?
F C Bint (1893-1898) was a pupil of ex-Sexey’s Headmaster W. Knight. His son, R J Bint (1927-1932) and his grandsons David (1966-1973) and Robert (1973-1980) Bint also attended Sexey’s School.

Careers
Careers preparation at Sexey’s School
At Sexey’s School we provide all our students in Years 7 to 13 with a comprehensive programme of careers preparation, education, information, advice and guidance (CEIAG) and work related learning (WRL) to complement their curriculum learning and prepare them for life after school.
We are exceptionally proud that we have been recognised for our Careers Programme achieving the highest marks available with 100% scores across the eight Gatsby benchmarks. These were developed on behalf of the Gatsby Foundation by Sir John Holman. They define what world-class careers provision in education looks like and provide a clear framework for organising the careers provision at schools or colleges.
You can find out more about our Careers Preparation Programme and Careers Policy here.
Use the links below to find details on local and national careers events and workshops, subject pathways and industry information, options for post 16 and higher education and useful resources for students and parents.
We welcome the help of local businesses to raise the career aspirations of our students, develop their employability skills, assist with mock interview days and give career or curriculum talks to help students learn more about the exciting industries in Somerset and the wide range of careers available.
